text:
kevin: Heads up — p95/p99 for hosted generation spiked around 09:12 UTC. Queue depth jumped ~3x and we saw a throughput plateau. Not seeing obvious DB or infra throttles.

opsbot: incident created #INC-2026-1783 (severity:minor) — alerted eng-runtime on-call.

maria: looking at metrics now. KV cache hit rate dropped from 0.62 -> 0.35 around the same time. Could be a cache churn or eviction pattern.

dmitri: interesting — kernel-selector logs show a recent heuristic flip at 09:10 that prefers "float32_attn_v2" for sequences >512 when latency budget allows. Could be a mismatch with quantized models.

liz: batch size distribution shifted toward lots of size=1 and size=2 requests starting 09:11. Batcher coalesce latency spiked. Likely explains p95 but not p99 entirely.

kevin: attaching quick dump from /admin/queue/stats:
```
queue_depth: 240 -> 720
avg_coalesce_ms: 3.2 -> 18.7
batch_size_p50: 8 -> 3
batch_size_p95: 32 -> 9
```

maria: profiler flamegraph from 09:14 (sampled): main hot paths are `batcher.coalesce_wait` and `kvcache.lookup_miss_path`. Also some time in `kernel_selector.evaluate_candidates`.

maria: paste:
```
# top stack samples
batcher.coalesce_wait 36%
kvcache.lookup_miss_path 22%
kernel_selector.evaluate 14%
runtime.dispatch 8%
```

dmitri: kernel_selector.evaluate at 14% is high. If we're frequently picking a slower kernel for mid-length sequences that used to pick quantized kernel, that would blow p99. Can we force kernel_override to `quantized_attn_v1` for the affected model as an experiment?

kevin: can try. Doing a hot override on model-prod/large-2025 now (scope: single cluster) — will route new requests to quantized_attn_v1 for 5m.

deploy-bot: hotpatch applied to model-prod/large-2025 -> kernel_override=quantized_attn_v1 (clusters: hosted-us-east-1).

liz: after override: coalesce median fell to 4.1ms and queue depth is back down to ~260. KV cache hit still low though (0.37). p95 dropped near baseline but p99 still ~1.6x baseline.

maria: low KV hit suggests many new prefixes — maybe a traffic shape change (more long-form chat or unique prompts). I pulled a 1k sample of requests; ~42% contain dynamic few-shot examples (unique per request). That explains cache misses.

dmitri: ok. Two contributing factors: batching fragmentation (small batches) and cache miss rate increasing tail latency. Kernel mismatch made it worse by picking float kernel in some cases. Override helped batching side; need to address KV churn.

kevin: short-term mitigation options: 1) pin kernel override (if stable) 2) increase small-batch coalesce window by +5ms for hosted tier (gives better batching) 3) temporary adaptive cache TTL bump for prefixes (reduce eviction). Thoughts?

liz: +1 to bump coalesce window; small increase won't harm p50 and helps p95. Be careful with throughput targets.

maria: adaptive cache TTL bump risky for memory pressure but can help p99. Maybe make it conditional for requests flagged as repeatable? Not trivial.

dmitri: we should also roll back the kernel-selector heuristic flip until we have perf test coverage for mixed-length traffic. I'll open a revert PR and block auto-apply for 24h.

kevin: actions:
- dmitri: revert heuristic flip PR and open follow-up with perf tests (ETA 2h)
- liz: bump coalesce window +5ms for hosted tier (hot config change) (ETA 10m)
- maria: investigate request shapes and suggest cache policy tweak (ETA 1h)
- kevin: monitor p95/p99 and queue depth; leave override in place for 30m then evaluate

opsbot: action items recorded in #oncall-runbook.

maria: one more datapoint — kernel selection miss-rate correlates with sequence length distribution shift: proportion of sequences 600-1200 tokens increased from 6% -> 22%. That triggers different kernel paths.

kevin: okay. If batcher/coalesce fix reduces small batches and revert removes regressive kernel picks, we should get p99 back. If not, we'll consider KV cache policy changes or a short-term admission control for very large sequences.

dmitri: starting revert PR now. I'll comment in the PR with perf benchmarks.

liz: applying coalesce window change in hosted-config now.
deploy-bot: config updated: hosted-tier.coalesce_window_ms = hosted-tier.coalesce_window_ms + 5 (rolled to 6/8 clusters).

kevin: monitoring — early signs: queue depth dropping, p95 improving, p99 trending down. Will update in 20m. Thanks team :thumbsup:

maria: I'll keep digging on KV access patterns and send a short report with sample prompts.

kevin: closing loop later. If anyone sees a new regression, ping here or escalate to on-call.

liz: noted.

opsbot: incident INC-2026-1783 set to monitoring.

kevin: follow-up — please add the profiling flamegraph to the incident ticket and tag `perf-regression` and `kvcache` labels.

maria: added artifacts to the ticket.

kevin: thanks all — moving to watch.
